title: Notch Filter - WiFi 6E (6 GHz) for Satellite L-Band Filter
subtitle: Design Validation and Performance Characterization
author: Dr. Ahmed Al-Farsi

sections.1_OBJECTIVE: This document describes the design, simulation, and characterization of a Notch Filter filter targeting WiFi 6E (6 GHz) for Satellite L-Band Filter. The filter is designed on Langasite substrate with a target center frequency of 3902.5 MHz and bandwidth of 139.8 MHz. The objective is to validate that the filter meets the required insertion loss, rejection, and linearity specifications for integration into the Satellite L-Band Filter module. This design iteration addresses feedback from the previous revision regarding out-of-band rejection improvements and temperature stability.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Filter Type: Notch Filter
- Frequency Band: WiFi 6E (6 GHz)
- Application: Satellite L-Band Filter
- Substrate: Langasite
- Package: CSP (Chip Scale Package)
- Design Tool: COMSOL Multiphysics 6.2
- Design Center: San Jose Advanced Design Lab

This specification applies to all variants of the Notch Filter design targeting WiFi 6E (6 GHz). Results are used to qualify the design for mass production release.
sections.3_DESIGN_PARAMETERS:
Center Frequency:       3902.5 MHz
Bandwidth (3 dB):       139.8 MHz
Insertion Loss Target:  <= 2.0 dB
Return Loss Target:     >= 14.0 dB
Out-of-Band Rejection:  >= 45.0 dB
Isolation (Duplexer):   >= 41.0 dB
Q Factor:               2860
Temperature Coefficient:-17.2 ppm/°C
Die Size:               1.5 x 1.2 mm
Wafer Size:             8-inch
Number of Resonators:   6
Electrode Material:     Mo/Al
Passivation:            Si3N4
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Open COMSOL Multiphysics 6.2 and load the Notch Filter template project.
2. Define the substrate stack: Langasite with specified layer thicknesses.
3. Set design targets: center freq 3902.5 MHz, BW 139.8 MHz.
4. Run initial EM simulation with 2D mesh density of 20 cells/wavelength.
5. Optimize resonator geometry using gradient descent (target IL < 2.0 dB).
6. Verify coupling coefficients between resonator stages.
7. Run 3D FEM simulation to account for package parasitics (CSP (Chip Scale Package)).
8. Export GDS-II layout for mask fabrication.
9. Fabricate prototype wafers (8-inch, Langasite).
10. Perform on-wafer probing using Rohde & Schwarz FSW Signal Analyzer.
11. Measure S-parameters (S11, S21, S12, S22) from 100 MHz to 11708 MHz.
12. Compare measured results against simulation and specification limits.
13. Perform temperature cycling (-40°C to +85°C) and re-measure.
14. Document results and generate summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Insertion loss at center frequency shall be <= 2.0 dB
- Return loss in passband shall be >= 14.0 dB
- Out-of-band rejection at +/- 210 MHz offset >= 45.0 dB
- Group delay variation across passband shall be <= 5 ns
- Temperature drift over -40°C to +85°C shall be <= 8.4 MHz
- Power handling shall be >= +34 dBm at 1 dB compression
- ESD tolerance >= 1000 V (HBM)
- Die yield on qualification lot >= 92%
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Measurement Date:       2025-04-14
Devices Tested:         53
Insertion Loss (meas):  1.68 dB
Return Loss (meas):     16.4 dB
Rejection (meas):       48.1 dB
Isolation (meas):       46.0 dB
Q Factor (meas):        2860
Group Delay Variation:  7.7 ns
Power Handling:         +34 dBm
Die Yield:              91.2%

Result Classification:  NEEDS REVIEW
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Notch Filter design demonstrated below-target performance for WiFi 6E (6 GHz).
b) Insertion loss met target specification.
c) Out-of-band rejection exceeded the minimum requirement.
d) Package parasitic effects were consistent with 3D EM model predictions.
e) Wafer-level uniformity was excellent (sigma < 1.5%).
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
1. Review near-band rejection margin for worst-case temperature.
2. Re-run EM simulation with refined mesh for better accuracy.
3. Schedule follow-up measurement after design tweak.
